# Dhruv Pal

> Computer Science and Engineering undergraduate specializing in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning at Lovely Professional University.

## Profile

Dhruv Pal is based in Punjab, India. His academic and project interests include applied machine learning, software development, systems programming, research, and technical product development. He expects to graduate in August 2028.

## Selected projects

- [Vendor Invoice Intelligence System](https://github.com/Dhruva105/Vendor-Invoice-Intelligence-System): Python, SQL, scikit-learn, SQLite, and Streamlit application for freight-cost estimation and invoice risk review.
- [Unix-like File System Recovery and Optimization Tool](https://github.com/Dhruva105/file-system-recovery-tool): C++17 virtual file system with inode-based structures, bitmap allocation, write-ahead journaling, an LRU block cache, consistency checking, and defragmentation.
- [Loan Eligibility and Risk Modeling](https://github.com/Dhruva105/loan-kiosk-model): cost-sensitive classification exploration with threshold optimization, SHAP/LIME explainability components, and a Flask API.
- [Intelligent Task Prioritizer](https://github.com/Dhruva105/Intelligent-Task-Prioritizer): Java Swing application using a custom Binary Min-Heap to prioritize tasks by deadline and importance.
- [BigInt C++ Library](https://github.com/Dhruva105/BigInt-CPP-Library): arbitrary-precision integer arithmetic library.
- [Heart Disease Prediction](https://github.com/Dhruva105/heart-disease-prediction): educational Streamlit project using a saved scikit-learn K-Nearest Neighbors model, one-hot feature alignment, and a saved StandardScaler. Its repository includes `heart.csv` (918 rows); upstream dataset provenance and evaluation metrics are not documented. It is not clinically validated or a medical diagnostic tool.

## Research

Co-author of “Adaptive Learning in the Cloud: AI-Driven Personalization and Accessibility in Modern Education,” with Suvankar Dey and Tanya Pal. Published in the International Journal of Multidisciplinary Educational Research, 2025, Volume 14, Issue 10(4), pages 62–68. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17501410).
